TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees – Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: February 3, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of Contracts in excess of $5 Million Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board of Trustees approval, under the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of: 1.
A change order to a contract with First Transit Inc. for campus shuttle services.
This is a time and material contract based on usage throughout the year .
The current contract expires 06/30/25 and the University of Rhode Island is seeking to exercise the renewal option and extend it for two years.
Based on current usage , the University anticipates needing an additional $3.6M to be added to the current Purchase Order (PO) value of $9.6 million.
The proposed increase does not materially change the contract and is based on anticipated increased usage and fuel consumption. 2.

A change order to a contract with marketing firm Katie Schibler & Associates, LLC, (KSA) that extends the contract for an additional five (5) months and increases the total obligation by an estimated $500,000.
This increase and extension does not materially change the nature of the contract.
Recommendation: In the case of First Transit Inc, the extension and increase are part of the original contract renewal options .
This change order is in line with the annual usage and prior spend of this contract and therefore the recommendation is to approve this change order.
KSA is a time and materials contract for media campaigns, marketing and advertising.
The contract is being extended while the solicitation and award of a new contract is in process.
It is also anticipated that some transition time will be necessary should there be a change in vendor.
This increase includes the previously Board of Trustees approved (February 16, 2024) costs for marketing and communications services for Human Resources and the Graduate School, both of which were previously under separate contracts.

Points to Consider: Each of the above contracts represents ongoing support services that are part of the current operations of the campus.
